cards.text: Isaiah the prophet is passing along words from the LORD (Isaiah 1:1), and now the LORD speaks about Assyria, a powerful nation. It opens with "Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger" right out of the gate. Friend, when a message opens with woe, you do NOT want your name right after it.

cards.question: The LORD calls Assyria the rod of His anger. What does He call the staff in their hands?

cards.text: Then God says He'll send Assyria against a godless nation, a people destined for His rage.

cards.question: God sends Assyria against a godless nation. True or false: He sends Assyria there to take spoils and seize plunder.

cards.text: God even sends him to trample them down like clay in the streets. But the LORD says this is not Assyria's intention, this is not his plan.

cards.question: God sends Assyria on His mission, but Assyria has a plan of his own. What's in his heart?

answers.text: To destroy and cut off many nations
To make peace with every nation
To bring the people back to God

cards.text: Then Assyria starts bragging: "Are not all my commanders kings?" Friend, I run a whole bakery and I just go by Papa, and this guy's MIDDLE MANAGERS are kings?
Then he pairs up cities: Calno like Carchemish, Hamath like Arpad, and "Is not Samaria like Damascus?" Friend, this man is reading his own highlight reel out loud.

cards.question: Assyria asks, "Is not Samaria like Damascus?" True or false: His point is that Samaria is tougher to take than Damascus.

cards.text: He says his hand has already seized idolatrous kingdoms. Then he sizes those kingdoms up against two more cities.

cards.question: Assyria brags about idolatrous kingdoms his hand already seized. What does he say those kingdoms had that surpassed what the two cities had?
Assyria says he's already done it to Samaria and its idols. So he asks: will I not also do it to ___ and her idols?

cards.text: Then the message turns. When the Lord has completed all His work against Mount Zion and Jerusalem, He will speak about the king of Assyria.

cards.question: Once His work against Jerusalem is done, the Lord will punish the king of Assyria for the fruit of his ___ heart.
The Lord quotes what the king of Assyria says about his victories. True or false: The king gives the LORD the credit for them.

cards.text: The king says, "By the strength of my hand I have done this, and by my wisdom, for I am clever." Friend, I stamped my own apron by accident TWICE this week, so I am in no position to say "for I am clever" about ANYTHING.
He keeps going: he's removed the boundaries of nations, plundered their treasures and subdued their rulers. He says his hand reached as into a nest to seize the wealth of the nations.

cards.question: The king says his hand reached as into a nest. He says he gathered all the earth like one gathering what?

cards.text: He even says no wing fluttered, no beak opened or chirped. Then comes the answer to all that bragging, and it's a question: "Does an axe raise itself above the one who swings it?"

cards.question: The passage asks, "Does an axe raise itself above the one who swings it?" True or false: The answer that question expects is no.

cards.text: "Does a saw boast over him who saws with it?" Friend, I'm a stamper, and if I'd ever stamped a cookie and turned to the hand holding me like, "You're WELCOME," I'd have ended up in a junk drawer a whole lot sooner than I did.
So the Lord GOD of Hosts will send a wasting disease among Assyria's stout warriors. And under all that pomp, He's got something else coming too.

cards.question: The passage speaks of the Light of Israel and its Holy One. That Light will become a ___.

cards.text: That fire will burn and devour Assyria's thorns and thistles. The splendor of its forests and orchards, both soul and body, will be completely destroyed, as a sickness consumes a man.

cards.question: True or false: The fire takes years to burn through Assyria's thorns and thistles.
When the fire is done, how many trees are left in Assyria's forests?

answers.text: So few a child could count them
Just enough to build one house
One left standing on each hill
